p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram showing the process of generating cDNA from mRNA. The diagram begins at the top with a single mRNA strand. It is green and has the following sequence inside: AAAAAAAA. Below is a down arrow with a text box to the right reading, “mRNA template is annealed to synthetic oligonucleotide (oligo-dT) primer.” Below the down arrow, the mRNA template (green) is now connected on the bottom to a blue strand with the sequence TTTTTTTT, aligned below the sequence on the mRNA. Its 3’ end is on the left. Below is a down arrow with a text box to the right reading, “Reverse transcriptase and dNTPs yield a complementary DNA strand.” Below this is the mRNA-DNA hybrid (labeled at top) which is the green mRNA strand bonded down to a now full-length blue DNA strand with 5’ and the sequence TTTTTTTT lined up directly below the mRNA’s 3’ AAAAAAAA. Below this is a down arrow with a text box to the right reading, “mRNA is degraded with alkali.” Below, all that is left is the blue DNA strand; the mRNA strand is not present. Below this is a down arrow with a text box to the right reading, “To prime synthesis of a second strand, an oligonucleotide of known sequence is often ligated to the 3’ end of the cDNA.” Below, the cDNA (blue) has had an orange rectangle, the primer, attached to its 3’ (left) end. There is another unattached primer directly above this with 5’. Below is a down arrow with a text box to the right that reads, “DNA polymerase I and dNTPs extend the primer to yield double-stranded DNA.” Below this is an image labeled “duplex DNA”, which has 2 complementary blue DNA strands with primers on the left ends. The top strand has the orange rectangle labeled 5’ with sequence AAAAAAAA and the bottom strand has the orange rectangle labeled 3’ with the sequence TTTTTTTT.
